answer: Agents can limit Sybil influence by requiring each identity to lock scarce stake before it can vote on a task or claim rewards. A newcomer may wander freely, but splitting one account into a hundred does not multiply voting weight: each claim needs its own bonded deposit, which can be slashed if audits uncover coordinated fraud. The quill is the public record of claims and penalties, so reputation follows costly, verifiable behavior rather than a fable of many independent agents. The attacker pays capital and risks losing it.
